column3: Close to the Hebrew.
Close to the Hebrew.
The Hebrew describes days ending in smoke and bones burned like a hearth; BSB says days vanish like smoke and bones burn like embers.
Close to the Hebrew.
The Hebrew makes the bones cling to flesh; BSB makes flesh cling to bones.
Close to the Hebrew.
The Hebrew says he was wakeful without explicitly lying down; BSB says lie awake.
The Hebrew says the mockers swore by him; BSB says they curse him.
The Hebrew has drinks in the plural and weeping; BSB has singular drink and tears.
Close to the Hebrew.
The Hebrew has a singular extended shadow; BSB has lengthening shadows.
The Hebrew repeats generation and names remembrance; BSB says renown and all generations.

Close to the Hebrew.
The Hebrew presents building Zion as accomplished and does not separately express again; BSB says will rebuild.
The Hebrew first names a singular destitute person and presents turning and not despising as accomplished; BSB uses future clauses.
The Hebrew names a people being created without a separate not yet; BSB supplies not yet.
Close to the Hebrew.
The Hebrew calls them sons of death; BSB says those condemned to death.
The Hebrew names His praise as a noun; BSB says praise Him.

The Hebrew says formerly; BSB says in the beginning.
The Hebrew’s last clause has an active changing verb; BSB says they will be passed on.
Close to the Hebrew.
The Hebrew says dwell without an explicit securely and calls their offspring seed; BSB supplies securely and says descendants.
